# API reference

     Do not edit by hand: `npm run docs:check` fails if this drifts from the code. -->

Everything below is reachable from the bundle's single `NotationEngine` global (or from `import ... from "notation-engine"`).

## Supported entry points

These are what a host application is meant to call. Everything in [the full index](#full-index) below is a building block the engine uses on itself: exported, usable and documented, but not covered by any stability promise.

### Rendering

#### `renderFromMusicXml`

```ts
export function renderFromMusicXml(xmlText: string, options?: RenderFromMusicXmlOptions): RenderFromMusicXmlResult;
```

Parse a MusicXML document and render it, in one call -- the ordinary entry point, and exactly `parseMusicXml` followed by `renderParsedMusicXml`.

*(`src/render-from-musicxml.ts`)*

#### `renderParsedMusicXml`

```ts
export function renderParsedMusicXml(parsed: ParseResult, options?: RenderParsedMusicXmlOptions): RenderFromMusicXmlResult;
```

Phase 53/§18.1: render a score that has ALREADY been parsed.

*(`src/render-from-musicxml.ts`)*

#### `parseMusicXml`

```ts
export function parseMusicXml(xmlText: string, options?: ParseMusicXmlOptions): ParseResult;
```

Turns a MusicXML `<score-partwise>` document into a `Score` (§6) plus the `MeasureAttributes` side-table and any `Diagnostic`s.

*(`src/parser/musicxml/parse.ts`)*

#### `unzipMxl`

```ts
export function unzipMxl(bytes: Uint8Array, domParser: new () => DomParserLike): UnzipMxlResult;
```

§10.2: a `.mxl` file is a ZIP archive.

*(`src/parser/musicxml/mxl.ts`)*

#### `parseMidiFile`

```ts
export function parseMidiFile(bytes: Uint8Array): ParseMidiResult;
```

§11: turns a `.mid` byte stream into a note list plus a tempo/meta timeline.

*(`src/parser/midi/parse.ts`)*

### Configuration

#### `resolveConfig`

```ts
export function resolveConfig(overrides?: PartialEngineConfig): EngineConfig;
```

Merges a partial config against DEFAULT_CONFIG, section by section -- every section not mentioned in `overrides` keeps its default wholesale, and every field not mentioned within a section that IS overridden keeps that section's default for just that field.

*(`src/config/config.ts`)*

#### `DEFAULT_CONFIG`

```ts
export const DEFAULT_CONFIG: EngineConfig;
```

Reasonable defaults for every section -- black ink on white, scroll layout at a modest pixel scale, notation-moves cursor sync (matching the earlier drum-video project's panning behavior), plain noteheads, straight beams, bar numbers at each system start, standard key signatures.

*(`src/config/config.ts`)*

### Playback and cursor

#### `getEventStream`

```ts
export function getEventStream(playback:
```

§17.1's own `getEventStream()` -- a plain accessor kept as an exported function (rather than reading `playback.events` directly) so the public shape matches the spec's own pseudocode exactly.

*(`src/playback/event-stream.ts`)*

#### `positionToX`

```ts
export function positionToX(playback: PlaybackData, tick: number): EventPosition;
```

§17.1: time -> where on the page.

*(`src/playback/position.ts`)*

#### `playheadX`

```ts
export function playheadX(playback: PlaybackData, tick: number): EventPosition;
```

§17.1, for a MOVING playhead: where the music is at `tick`, as a continuous position rather than the last note's own x.

*(`src/playback/position.ts`)*

#### `xToPosition`

```ts
export function xToPosition(playback: PlaybackData, x: number, systemIndex: number): number;
```

§17.1: where on the page -> time, for click-to-seek in a host app.

*(`src/playback/position.ts`)*

#### `resolvePosition`

```ts
export function resolvePosition(playback: PlaybackData, tick: number): PlaybackPosition;
```

§17.1's `PlaybackPosition` for an arbitrary tick -- tick, real seconds (§12's tempo map) and measure+beat, all three views of the same instant.

*(`src/playback/position.ts`)*

#### `computeCursorPlacement`

```ts

```

PLAN.md §17.2, Phase 49.

*(`src/playback/cursor.ts`)*

#### `renderCursor`

```ts
export function renderCursor(placement: CursorPlacement, options: RenderCursorOptions): string;
```

PLAN.md §17.2, Phase 49: draws the cursor marker itself.

*(`src/render/cursor.ts`)*

#### `notationEventId`

```ts
export function notationEventId(partId: string, measureNumber: number, voiceId: number, eventIndex: number): string;
```

The id of ONE notated event -- the `data-id` its `<g>` carries in the rendered SVG (Phase 51/§18.3) and the stem every `noteIds` entry below is built from.

*(`src/playback/event-stream.ts`)*

#### `elementIdForNoteId`

```ts
export function elementIdForNoteId(noteId: string): string;
```

The rendered element a `noteId` belongs to: a chord member's `...#e3#n1` lives inside the chord's own `...#e3` group, since a chord is drawn as one element with several noteheads.

*(`src/playback/event-stream.ts`)*

### Repeats (playback order)

#### `performanceSecondsToWritten`

```ts
export function performanceSecondsToWritten(plan: RepeatPlan, tempoMap: TempoMap, seconds: number): PerformancePoint;
```

Maps a moment of audio playback (seconds from the start of the performance) onto the written tick sounding then.

*(`src/playback/repeats.ts`)*

#### `performanceTickToWritten`

```ts
export function performanceTickToWritten(plan: RepeatPlan, performanceTick: number): PerformancePoint;
```

Maps a tick in performance order onto the written tick it plays.

*(`src/playback/repeats.ts`)*

#### `writtenTickToPerformanceTicks`

```ts
export function writtenTickToPerformanceTicks(plan: RepeatPlan, writtenTick: number): readonly number[];
```

Every performance tick at which `writtenTick` is played -- the inverse of `performanceTickToWritten`, which is one-to-many exactly because a repeated bar is played more than once.

*(`src/playback/repeats.ts`)*

#### `buildRepeatPlan`

```ts
export function buildRepeatPlan(input: BuildRepeatPlanInput):
```

Unfolds a score's repeats into a `RepeatPlan`: for every measure, every time it is played, where that playing sits in performance time and which written measure it is.

*(`src/playback/repeats.ts`)*


§16.3's re-flow decision: page mode's system breaking depends on the USABLE width available (§16.2's own `pageWidth - margins`), so a resize whose new width would place a different set of measures into each system needs the real layout algorithms re-run from the cached `Score`, not just a pixel-a...

#### `extractViewBox`

```ts
export function extractViewBox(svg: string): ViewBox | undefined;
```

Extracts an existing `<svg>` document's own `viewBox` dimensions -- the content's natural size in staff-space units, unaffected by whatever `width`/`height` pixel attributes it currently carries.

*(`src/layout/resize.ts`)*

#### `computePxPerStaffSpace`

```ts
export function computePxPerStaffSpace(viewBox: ViewBox, targetWidthPx: number, targetHeightPx: number): number;
```

§16.3's pure-scale computation: given the content's own natural `viewBox` and a target pixel size, computes the single `pxPerStaffSpace` that fits the content within that box while preserving its own aspect ratio (the SAME convention `object-fit: contain` uses) -- the smaller of the two possible ...

*(`src/layout/resize.ts`)*

### Debug

#### `measureSvgBoxes`

```ts
export function measureSvgBoxes(svg: string): readonly DebugBox[];
```

Every drawn element in `svg`, as a bounding box in staff-space units.

*(`src/debug/measure.ts`)*

#### `computeDebugSkylines`

```ts
export function computeDebugSkylines(boxes: readonly DebugBox[], staffBottomYs: readonly number[], sampleWidth?: number): readonly DebugStaffSkyline[];
```

One north and one south skyline per staff, from the measured boxes.

*(`src/debug/skyline.ts`)*

#### `renderBoundingBoxOverlay`

```ts
export function renderBoundingBoxOverlay(boxes: readonly OverlayBox[], options: RenderBoundingBoxOverlayOptions): string;
```

One stroked rectangle per box, in a single `<g class="debug-bounding-boxes">` so a host can hide the whole overlay with one CSS rule.

*(`src/render/debug-overlay.ts`)*

#### `renderSkylineOverlay`

```ts
export function renderSkylineOverlay(skylines: readonly OverlaySkyline[], options: RenderSkylineOverlayOptions): string;
```

Both sides of every staff's skyline, in one `<g class="debug-skyline">`.

*(`src/render/debug-overlay.ts`)*

#### `filterDiagnostics`

```ts
export function filterDiagnostics<T extends HasSeverity>(diagnostics: readonly T[], level: LogLevel): readonly T[];
```

The diagnostics `level` lets through, in their original order.

*(`src/debug/log-level.ts`)*

### `src/core/duration-math.ts`

| | Name | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| const | `TICKS_PER_QUARTER` | The engine's internal tick resolution: how many ticks make up one quarter note, REGARDLESS of what <divisions> value the source MusicXML used. |
| function | `baseTicksForType` | The base tick length of a duration type, with no dots and no tuplet applied. |
| function | `ticksWithDots` | Dotted-note expansion: each dot adds half of what the previous dot (or the base note, for the first dot) added. |
| function | `applyTuplet` | A tuplet ratio scales ticks down: `actualNotes` notes fill the time `normalNotes` of them normally would, so each actual note is shorter by a factor of normalNotes/actualNotes (e.g. a standard triplet: 3 actual notes in the time of 2 normal ones, so each is 2/3 its written length). |
| function | `ticksForDisplayedDuration` | The full displayed-duration tick length: base type + dots + tuplet. |
| function | `durationTypeAndDotsFromTicks` | The inverse of ticksForDisplayedDuration() for the no-tuplet case: given a tick length, find the (type, dots) pair that produces it exactly (or within floating-point tolerance). |
| function | `xmlDivisionsToTicks` | Converts a raw MusicXML <duration> value into the engine's normalized ticks (see TICKS_PER_QUARTER above), given that XML file's own <divisions> (ticks-per-quarter-note in ITS units, which the parser reads per-part and which can even change mid-piece in a pathological file). |
| function | `ticksToXmlDivisions` | The inverse of xmlDivisionsToTicks() -- e.g. useful later for Phase 49's export. |
| function | `sumTicks` | Sums a sequence of Durations' authoritative tick lengths -- e.g. a chain of tied notes' total sounding length. |
